item: Cupertino composite ad valorem rate 1.1636% (FY2025-26)
why_flagged: Derived by summing the county, school, college and district rates from the Santa Clara County Tax Rate Book summary pages; the parcel's own tax-rate-area table (13-xxx) could not be read (PDF beyond the fetch tool's 30-page limit).
impact: Low: at most +0.002% (El Camino Hospital District) difference; direct charges are separate.
what_would_resolve_it: Open the parcel's tax bill or the rate book TRA table for the parcel's TRA.

item: Property A direct charges about $930/yr (2025)
why_flagged: Computed as the user-supplied bill ($7,210) minus 1.1636% x user-supplied assessed value ($539,740). Individual parcel taxes (school, library, water, etc.) were not itemised.
impact: Low (about $1,000/yr).
what_would_resolve_it: Read the 'special assessments / direct charges' section of the 2025-26 tax bill.

item: Property B fixed charges $1,000/yr
why_flagged: No bill line items available; SF parcels carry several voter-approved parcel taxes and fees.
impact: Low-moderate (hundreds to about $2,000/yr).
what_would_resolve_it: Read the SF secured tax bill for the parcel.

item: Insurance premiums ($1,500/yr each property)
why_flagged: User guesses. The CA Department of Insurance premium comparison tool is interactive and could not be read; no official premium for 95014 or 94122 was obtained. A 3-unit SF landlord policy may cost well above $1,500.
impact: Moderate: insurance is the fastest-growing cost line in the model (5%/yr assumed).
what_would_resolve_it: Run the CDI homeowners premium comparison for 95014 (HO-3, owner-occupied) and 94122 (dwelling fire / landlord, 3 units) or obtain broker quotes.

item: Maintenance and repairs ($6,000/yr A; $12,000/yr B in 2026 dollars)
why_flagged: No official source exists for a specific property's maintenance cost; figures are model assumptions grown with CPI.
impact: Moderate over 30 years.
what_would_resolve_it: Replace with actual expense history from the transferor's records.

item: Property B build year and rent-control status
why_flagged: Not supplied. If the certificate of occupancy pre-dates June 14 1979 the two occupied units are rent-controlled (1.6% allowable increase 2026-27) with just-cause eviction; the model assumes they are.
impact: High for the rental scenarios: controlled rents grow about half as fast as market rents and owner move-in is restricted.
what_would_resolve_it: Check the SF Assessor record / Rent Board for the building's year built and any exemptions.

item: Which property is the Transferor's principal residence
why_flagged: The model assumes Property A (Cupertino). If the Transferor instead lives in a unit of Property B, the Prop 19 exclusion would apply to that unit (1/3 of B) and Property A would be fully reassessed.
impact: High: determines which property can keep a low assessed value.
what_would_resolve_it: Confirm where the Homeowners' Exemption is currently claimed (it can only be claimed on one home).

item: Ownership structure of both properties (100% in a revocable trust assumed)
why_flagged: If either property is already partly owned by the Heir, held in an LLC/partnership, or co-owned with non-family members, the change-in-ownership, step-up and Prop 19 results differ.
impact: High for tax basis and reassessment.
what_would_resolve_it: Review the trust instrument and vesting deeds with an estate attorney.

item: Year-by-year assessment histories withheld from the public repository
why_flagged: Exact assessed values are quasi-identifiers (searchable on public rolls). Only a rounded 2025 anchor for Property A and a derived ratio for Property B are kept.
impact: Low for the heir's decision: B is reassessed to market at inheritance; A's series is anchored on 2025.
what_would_resolve_it: None needed; keep private copies offline.

item: Residential rental depreciation period (27.5-year straight line)
why_flagged: Stated in IRS Publication 527 but the specific table was not re-read in this session (the publication's table of contents was fetched).
impact: Low (affects rental-scenario income tax only).
what_would_resolve_it: Open Pub. 527 chapter 2 (MACRS, residential rental property).

item: 'Repeal the Death Tax' initiative signature counts
why_flagged: The failure to qualify is consistent with the SOS qualified-measures list, but the signature figures (about 560,000 of 874,641) come from news reports found by web search.
impact: Low (initiative is not on any ballot).
what_would_resolve_it: Check the SOS initiative status page history.

item: November 3 2026 election results are unofficial
why_flagged: Prop 3 (passed), Prop 40 (failed) and Prop 42 (leading) figures are from the Secretary of State's unofficial returns as of Nov 9 2026; certification is due Dec 11 2026.
impact: Low-moderate for long-run California income tax rates.
what_would_resolve_it: Re-check certified results after Dec 11 2026.

item: No City of Cupertino transfer tax
why_flagged: Only the county rate ($1.10 per $1,000; Rev. & Tax. Code 11911) was verified; a Cupertino municipal page confirming the absence of a city tax was not found.
impact: Low (about $3,400 on a $3.1M sale).
what_would_resolve_it: Confirm with the Santa Clara County Clerk-Recorder fee schedule.

item: San Francisco Empty Homes Tax could be revived
why_flagged: Struck down by the Superior Court (2024) and Court of Appeal (Sept 11 2026); a California Supreme Court petition is possible.
impact: Moderate if revived and a B unit is left vacant.
what_would_resolve_it: Monitor the Treasurer's EHT page; keep all units occupied.

item: Market values ($3,100,000 A; $1,800,000 B as of Nov 2026)
why_flagged: User estimates, not appraisals. All projections scale with these.
impact: High: every dollar figure in the projections scales with them.
what_would_resolve_it: Date-of-death appraisal (required anyway for the step-up and Prop 19).

item: Property B effective property-tax rate about 2.14% of assessed value
why_flagged: Far above the 1.18% ad valorem rate. This is consistent with a very low Prop 13 base plus fixed parcel charges, but could also indicate a data-entry mismatch (e.g., bill and assessed value from different years).
impact: Low for the heir (B is reassessed at inheritance).
what_would_resolve_it: Compare one year's bill with the same year's assessed value.

item: Property A effective rate 1.335% vs composite 1.1636%
why_flagged: Implies about $930 of direct charges; plausible for Cupertino (school/college parcel taxes) but unverified.
impact: Low.
what_would_resolve_it: Read the bill's direct-charge lines.

item: GitHub Pages was publishing an empty README-only site from main:/
why_flagged: At the start of the project the repository contained only 'README.md' ('# Tino1') and Pages was enabled from the root of main, so the live URL showed a near-empty page. The site is now built in /docs with a .nojekyll file; the Pages source must point at /docs.
impact: None once the Pages source is switched.
what_would_resolve_it: Confirmed in the integration step (see COORDINATION.md).

item: Market rent for Property A ($6,390/month in 2026)
why_flagged: HUD's 40th-percentile Small Area FMR for a 4-bedroom in 95014; actual market rent for a $3.1M home is probably higher, so the rent-A scenarios are conservative.
impact: Moderate for S3/S5.
what_would_resolve_it: Obtain a local rental comparables report.

item: Water/sewer and electricity figures
why_flagged: User-supplied ranges (A $100-150; B $330-400 water; B $30-70 electricity); utility rate schedules were not read.
impact: Low.
what_would_resolve_it: Check SFPUC and the Cupertino water retailer's current rate schedules.

item: 2026-27 assessed-value inflation factor of 2% for Property A
why_flagged: The constitutional maximum; the actual BOE-announced CCPI factor for the 2026 roll was not fetched.
impact: Negligible.
what_would_resolve_it: BOE Letter To Assessors on the annual inflation factor.

item: Heir's income-tax position
why_flagged: Combined marginal rates (37.1% on gains and net rent; 41.1% on depreciation recapture; 30% on portfolio gains at liquidation) assume a high-income California resident heir filing single.
impact: Moderate for after-tax comparisons; does not change the ranking in most sensitivity cases.
what_would_resolve_it: Replace with the heir's actual bracket and filing status.

item: Future economic parameters
why_flagged: Appreciation (A 4%, B 3%), rent growth (3% market / 1.6% controlled), CPI 2.5%, utilities 4%, insurance 5%, portfolio 7%, Prop 19 cap 2%, estate exclusion indexation 2.5% are assumptions anchored on the cited BLS, FHFA, Treasury and BOE figures.
impact: High: the ranking of 'keep A' vs 'sell A' flips at high appreciation / low returns (see sensitivity table).
what_would_resolve_it: Re-run analysis/model.py with updated parameters.
